This appears to come from an AD/CVD scope or CBP ruling on "steel liquid containment barriers." The likely classification is 7308.90 (structures of iron or steel and parts, other), so the question is which 10-digit statistical suffix applies.

Other candidates are 8479.89 (machines with individual functions) and 8481 (valves). A flap that closes automatically on liquid is not really a valve, since it does not control flow in a pipe. It is a structure installed in a door opening, which fits 7308.90. The 7308.90 subheadings are 7308.90.30 (clad/coated?), 7308.90.60 (other, 7308.90.6000), and 7308.90.95 (other: 7308.90.9590). Most "other" structures fall under 7308.90.9590.

The scope language "installed flush with the floor in front of or within an opening" resembles door/gate structures. Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds are 7308.30.50 (other). That heading covers "doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors." A flood barrier could be classed there, but since this one is described as a containment barrier with a floor housing, I'll go with 7308.90.9590.

```json
{"hts_code": "7308.90.9590", "reason": "The steel spill barriers are fabricated steel structures with a flap, side posts and floor housing, installed in openings and operated without power, so they fall under other structures and parts of iron or steel in heading 7308."}
```
